newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs stumble but will not fall.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs stumble but will not fall.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds faded after a strong morning session on Wednesday, stumbling into the red in the afternoon in a welcome but modest correction which traders said would be short lived.
"This is just what we needed, we were getting too strong," one trader said. "But soon the market will be heading higher again," he added.

At 1508 GMT, the new benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.84 percent against 5.77 percent in the morning and Tuesday's 5.81 close. "Some Belgian banks are selling and at these levels London is not buying," one trader said.
The yield premium of 10-year OLOs over equivalent Bunds widened to eight basis points against just two in the morning and four on Tuesday. It briefly went up to nine in early afternoon.

Traders said that compared with France and the Netherlands, Belgian bonds could not be considered expensive. "Certainly not against France," one said, noting the yield differential of 18 basis points between France and Belgium.
He noted that OLO markets were very volatile, which might be a bad omen as it followed a long uptrend. "It might, but we don't think (the market will crash)," he said.
Other traders were more optimistic and did not exclude that the OLO/Bund yield spread could easily dip below zero.
"A lot of Belgian banks cannot switch (out of Belgian OLOs), have to buy Belgian paper and are loaded with cash for the moment," one said.
He noted that the yield spread was already negative for most OLOs up to nine years.
